correctness.rationale: For fixed positive alpha and sufficiently large n, every prime in the window exceeds square-root n, so Legendre's formula collapses exactly to floor(n/p). The condition floor(n/p)=j is the interval n/(j+1)<p<=n/j, leaving only finitely many cells. Summing log p on each fixed positive-scaled interval and applying the prime number theorem gives the coefficient formula. The aligned top-window harmonic simplification and parity comparison are immediate finite sums. The bundled verifier independently confirms the exact cell regrouping in 250 finite cases and the predicted top-window profile numerically.

originality.rationale: Ma's recent theorem proves equal residue mass on fixed power bands, a scale whose total mass is of order n log n; its fixed-endpoint theorem does not imply a window with endpoints proportional to n, whose mass is only order n. Older valuation-pattern papers vary n for fixed primes and therefore have different quantifiers. No inspected or Resultary source gives the explicit piecewise-harmonic linear-window law or the parity bias. The result survives best-of-knowledge originality despite its classical proof ingredients.
residual_risks: Because the proof uses classical Legendre and prime-number-theorem ingredients, an equivalent boundary formula may exist under different terminology in analytic number theory.

value.rationale: The result identifies the natural boundary scale at which the recent fixed-power-band equidistribution ceases to look uniform and quantifies the resulting bias exactly. The explicit 3/5 versus 2/5 split is a concrete obstruction to unjustified uniform extrapolation and the general coefficient is reusable for any fixed linear window.

final_claim: For primes in any fixed linear window alpha*n < p <= beta*n, the weighted factorial-valuation mass in each residue class modulo a fixed h has the explicit finite piecewise-harmonic first-order coefficient stated in the package; in particular the window n/3 < p <= n has limiting odd/even weighted shares 3/5 and 2/5.
limitations: All parameters h, alpha and beta are fixed as n tends to infinity.
No uniform transition is claimed when the lower endpoint shrinks or h grows with n.
